_comment: Planting rules are offsets from your average last-spring frost (negative = before) or first-fall frost, in weeks. All dates are targets, not guarantees; soil temp and local experience win.

crops.name: Tomatoes
crops.tip: Transplant after nights stay above 50F; bury the stem deep for stronger roots.

crops.name: Peppers
crops.tip: Peppers hate cold feet - wait until soil is genuinely warm, not just air.

crops.name: Eggplant
crops.tip: Warm soil (60F+) or it sulks; black plastic mulch helps in cool climates.

crops.name: Cucumbers
crops.tip: Give a trellis and consistent water; bitter fruit usually means thirsty plants.

crops.name: Zucchini & Summer Squash
crops.tip: Two plants is plenty for most households; three is a joke you'll regret in August.

crops.name: Green Beans (bush)
crops.tip: Direct sow - beans resent transplanting. Pick every couple days to keep them producing.

crops.name: Sweet Potatoes
crops.tip: Slips want a long, hot season; a warm mulch and 4+ hours of sun pays off.

crops.name: Corn
crops.tip: Plant in a block, not a row - it's wind pollinated.

crops.name: Melons
crops.tip: Pinch to 2-3 fruits per vine in short-season climates for earlier harvests.

crops.name: Okra
crops.tip: Okra loves heat the way peas hate it - it takes off when nothing else will.

crops.name: Basil
crops.tip: Pinch flower buds to keep leaves coming; one plant flowers, the season's over.

crops.name: Cilantro
crops.tip: Bolts in heat - sow again in late summer for a fall crop.

crops.name: Lettuce & Salad Greens
crops.tip: One of the few crops you can sow right up to (and a bit past) your last frost.

crops.name: Spinach
crops.tip: Prefers cool soil; fall sowing overwinters under leaves for earliest spring picking.

crops.name: Kale & Collards
crops.tip: Flavor sweetens after a frost; spring and fall are their glory seasons.

crops.name: Carrots
crops.tip: Keep the seedbed damp for 10 days or you get empty rows; thin early and eat the thinnings.

crops.name: Beets & Chard
crops.tip: Each 'seed' is a cluster - thin to one seedling per spot.

crops.name: Radishes
crops.tip: Fastest crop in the garden - sow small batches every 2 weeks.

crops.name: Turnips & Rutabaga
crops.tip: A classic fall root; tops are as good as the roots.

crops.name: Peas (snap & shelling)
crops.tip: As soon as soil works - they'll take frost. Trellis early, before they tangle.

crops.name: Broccoli & Cauliflower
crops.tip: A fall crop grown in summer - start now for Sept harvests in many climates.

crops.name: Cabbage & Brussels Sprouts
crops.tip: Brussels sprouts improve after frost; spray for cabbage worms weekly.

crops.name: Onions & Leeks
crops.tip: Long-day vs short-day varieties matter more than almost anything else - match your latitude.

crops.name: Garlic (fall planting)
crops.tip: Clove point up, 2 inches deep, 6 inches apart; mulch heavily and wait until summer.

crops.name: Potatoes
crops.tip: Hill soil around stems as they grow; keep out of light or they turn green.

crops.name: Asparagus & Rhubarb
crops.tip: A 20-year investment - plant crowns in deep compost and never rush it.

crops.name: Strawberries
crops.tip: June-bearing runners spread fast; pin them down now for free plants next year.

crops.name: Roses, Coneflower & Pollinator Perennials
crops.tip: Fall is ideal planting weather for perennials - roots grow while tops rest.

crops.name: Tulips & Daffodils
crops.tip: Bulbs want soil that's genuinely cool; pointy end up, 3x the bulb's height deep.
